title: False-Positive-Aware, Destination-Centric DDoS Detection and Source-Scoped Mitigation in Software-Defined Networks
authors: Advait Pathak (23bcs094), Venkatesh Dhangar (23bcs041), Shantanu Dukare (23bcs121), Ojas Jogdand (23bds039), Dhanraj Matke (23bcs042)
tool: Google Deep Review (https://research.google/deepreview/), Gemini 4 Argon, Medium depth

rounds.custom_context: IEEE conference paper (course research project) on ML-based DDoS detection and mitigation in SDN, evaluated on a Mininet/Ryu testbed. Please check the mathematical formulation, the experimental methodology and baselines, the statistical validity of the results, and whether the claims are supported by the evidence.
new_experiments: Fresh seed 3 with the frozen final configuration: one detection-only and one mitigation session (shuffled attack order, 60 s gaps)
Calibration session repeated at the 25 Mbit/s test capacity (sensitivity analysis)
Offline ablation: Levels 2+3 without the flow model, refitted on the calibration session
Offline: fast-path parity for all baselines, survivorship-free (penalised) latency, per-role false-positive rates
Live-attribution diagnosis per attacker and episode (diagnose_attribution.py) and carry-over accounting (rules active at onset)

items.comment: Missing architectural ablation without the Level-1 flow classifier; the claim that gains come from Levels 2-3 is unverified.
items.response: Added the ablation (Levels 2+3 only, window and source models refitted without the six flow-ML features on the same calibration data). Pooled seed 2: F1 0.78 -> 0.73 and 21 % more false-positive windows; seed 3: 0.73 -> 0.71. The claim was corrected: most of the gain comes from Levels 2-3, but Level 1 contributes about 0.04 F1.
items.where: Sec. VI-B, Table III, Table VI, Conclusion

items.comment: Mitigation optimisation is ill-posed: goodput not a function of B_v, unit mismatch between packet rates and C_v (bit/s), R_max not enforced, port quarantine missing.
items.response: Rewrote the mitigation problem: offered bit rate l = lambda * mean packet size; goodput under proportional sharing of the bottleneck as an explicit function of the blocked set B and quarantined ports Q; no hard capacity constraint (an overloaded link lowers goodput instead of making B infeasible); equivalence to minimising residual attack load stated; R_max = 64 per destination and 64 per window documented as implemented (ranking by source score, rate-rule hits first); Q added for spoofed sources.

items.comment: Detection problem degenerates if (k, n, eta_f) are free; single-window quantile does not bound the confirmation false-alarm rate; continuous time vs window index; distribution of E[D] unspecified.
items.response: (k, n, eta_f) are now stated as fixed design parameters and only eta is optimised; the constraint is written on the single-window exceedance and the text says explicitly that it does not bound confirmation-level false alarms, which are reported empirically (FA/h); D is defined with window completion times t*Delta; E is the empirical mean over test episodes (not Lorden's worst case). Calibration 'segment' is defined.

items.comment: Counter-delta correction for re-installed entries is not formalised; switch index missing; asynchronous polling.
items.response: Eq. (1) is now a piecewise definition per switch sigma using the OpenFlow entry age delta and reply interval e: plain difference if the counter did not fall (covers re-added entries), otherwise counter * min(1, e/delta); first-seen entries; max over the path; rate divided by the largest reply interval, with the polling-jitter caveat stated.

items.comment: Latency lower bound ignores the fast path and repeat-offender trigger, pre-attack exceedances and sub-window accumulation; contradicts measured 1.2-1.3 s latencies.
items.response: The bound is rescoped to pure k-of-n confirmation under stated assumptions (no pre-attack exceedance, first window crosses eta); the text explains that the fast path, repeat offenders or a pre-attack exceedance reduce D to as little as U*Delta, and that an insufficient first window adds Delta. Table IV footnote points to this.

items.comment: Boundary singularities and missing formulas for entropy, response ratio, log rate change, rate jump, active windows.
items.response: Added Table I with the exact definition of all 19 destination and 10 pair features, the boundary conventions used in the code (H_d = 0 if n_d <= 1; ratios with max(.,1) and a cap of 10; +1 smoothing in log ratios; 0 when nothing is scored) and the multi-feature group counts.

items.comment: Abstract: report precision, distinguish realised FPR from the calibration budget, note that cross-dataset failure is bidirectional.
items.response: Abstract rewritten: 0.42 and 0.47 in both directions; recall 0.97, precision 0.65, F1 0.78 at a realised 0.26 % FPR with a 0.3 % budget.

items.comment: Undefined 'src' in the spoofing definition.
items.response: Now written as s != beta(sigma, p).

items.comment: Incomplete state machine: no RECOVERING -> NORMAL, SUSPECTED and MITIGATING never assigned, quiet-window predicate and episode counter undefined, quiet check unscoped.
items.response: Algorithm 1 rewritten with every transition used by the code (NORMAL/SUSPECTED/CONFIRMED/MITIGATING/RECOVERING), the over predicate o_d(t) (score >= eta, or >= 30 pps hitting drop rules while MITIGATING), the quiet counter scoped to CONFIRMED/MITIGATING, Q_e = 3 * 2^min(e_d - 1, 3), and when e_d is incremented (entering MITIGATING; never reset).

items.comment: Persistence and repeat offenders missing from Eq. (7); R_d predicate unspecified; attribution gated on s_d >= eta; cold-start and slow-ramp cases.
items.response: Eq. (9) now defines the instantaneous candidate set B~_d(t) and Eq. (10) the persistence-filtered B_d(t) = (B~(t) and B~(t')) or (B~(t) and R_d(t)); R_d(t) defined (blocked within 300 s and rate >= 15 pps); the gate is explained (o_d includes drop-rule hits); a new 'Edge cases' paragraph states the cold-start and slow-ramp weaknesses.

items.comment: Are drop-rule counters used for quiet windows? Hard timeout vs episode length; anti-spoofing binding, priority, timeout, scope.
items.response: Stated that drop-rule hit rates keep the episode open (part of o_d), that rules are removed on RECOVERING and re-installed if they expire while the attack continues, that the port binding is static topology configuration (cannot be poisoned by a first spoofed packet), quarantine priority 205 and hard timeout 300 s, independent of destination state, and that no allow rule is installed (limitation). Figure 1 caption updated.

items.comment: Exact subset of features that receive log(1+x).
items.response: Marked with a dagger in Table I; all are non-negative counts or rates.

items.comment: Figure 1 says per-source instead of per-pair features.
items.response: Figure regenerated with 'per-pair'.

items.comment: corr(s) depends on d; time indices; set notation for a single state; phi_{s,d} computed for all pairs.
items.response: Now corr_{s,d}(t) with time indices on lambda, r, s_d, B_d; 'state_d = NORMAL'; features are computed for every active pair because the baselines mu_{s,d} must be learned before an attack.

items.comment: Symbol epsilon overloaded for window and source thresholds.
items.response: Source budget renamed epsilon_s = 1 %.

items.comment: Victim capacity 50 Mbit/s in calibration vs 25 Mbit/s in test; pooled vs stratified quantile.
items.response: Rationale stated (the emulator delivers only 6-7 kpps of the 11 kpps offered, so 50 Mbit/s never saturated). Calibration was repeated at 25 Mbit/s: thresholds change (eta 0.844 -> 0.980) and the detector improves on all three held-out sessions (F1 0.80/0.82/0.78, FPR within the 0.3 % budget); destination entropy ties on one session but misses 4 of 27 episodes; conclusion: calibrate at the operating capacity and set eta_f relative to eta. The threshold is now stated to be a pooled quantile, and Table V gives the per-role FPR: 0 % on about 38,000 client windows but 24-30 % on the victim server's benign windows (none in the pre-attack benign period).
items.where: Sec. V-B, IV-E, VI-B (Table V), VI-G (Table X), Abstract
items.status: Resolved (new experiment); per-role calibration left as future work

items.comment: CIC-DDoS2019 has only 16,733 benign flows; grouping variable; deduplication scope; class-balanced prior.
items.response: Added: groups (bidirectional 5-tuple + protocol; day x minute x destination port for IDS2018); conflicting-label rows removed over the whole dataset before the split (stated as using holdout labels); same-label duplicates kept; only 13,386 benign CIC-DDoS2019 flows in the training split, all used, no oversampling; holdout has 569 benign; p_f not recalibrated from the 1:1 prior.

items.comment: Latency comparison is asymmetric (fast path only for the proposed method); source-entropy definition and direction.
items.response: Every baseline was re-evaluated with a single-window fast path at the same calibration exceedance rate (0.24 %) as eta_f; Table III reports both. The proposed detector remains fastest (3.2 s vs 4.5-11.9 s penalised). Source entropy is defined as unnormalised entropy in bits with an upper-tail alarm, and the choice is justified.

items.comment: Which edge switch hosts the victim and servers.
items.response: Stated: the last edge switch hosts h200, h198, h199, two attackers and five clients.

items.comment: Attribution rules were tuned on the held-out seed-2 schedule (data snooping); v1 covered only 5 segments.
items.response: Ran a fresh seed 3 once with the frozen configuration. Zero collateral holds out of sample (0 legitimate hosts blocked); detection keeps the best F1 (0.73). The mitigation benefit is smaller (HTTP 44 % -> 60 %), reported as such. The seed-2 zero-collateral result is now labelled in-sample. items.comment: Sequential episodes confound per-attack metrics (carry-over of collapse and of 300 s rules; low-rate 0.06 -> 1.00 with 0 rules).
items.response: Tables VII and VIII now separate new rules from attackers already blocked at onset; the text states that the low-rate gain is avoided collapse, not mitigation (low-rate is detected but not attributed), and gives the average over the five attacks with mainly active mitigation (69 % -> 86 %). Seed 3 uses a shuffled order and 60 s gaps (> 48 s maximum hold-down) to reduce carry-over.

items.comment: Diagnose why live ICMP attribution blocks 1/40 vs 38/40 offline.
items.response: Diagnosed by stepping the live configuration through the session telemetry: on seed 2, 36 of 40 ICMP attackers were already blocked at onset by all-protocol rules from the SYN episode (the original explanation was wrong). On seed 3, 28 of 40 ICMP attackers had no flow counters at all because the flood prevented flow setup. The remaining seed-2 service loss is reported as unexplained.
items.status: Resolved (root cause found); one residual effect unexplained

rounds.custom_context: Revision 1 of an IEEE conference paper (course research project) on ML-based DDoS detection and mitigation in SDN, evaluated on a Mininet/Ryu testbed. This revision added a fresh-seed validation, an ablation without the flow model, fast-path parity for baselines, a recalibration at the test link capacity, and a rewritten formulation and algorithm. Please check the mathematical formulation, the methodology and baselines, the statistical validity of the results, and whether the claims are supported by the evidence.
rounds.summary: Deep Review judged the round-1 revision to have rigorous experimental hygiene and transparency, and raised mainly consistency, specification and statistical-alignment issues. No new emulation runs were needed; one flow-model re-evaluation and one offline analysis on logged telemetry were added.
new_experiments: Flow model re-evaluated with label conflicts removed inside the training split only (holdouts untouched); ROC-AUC, cross-split duplicate share and balanced accuracy without duplicates; per-dataset paired bootstrap of balanced accuracy replacing the pooled McNemar test; model sizes
Offline on the three held-out detection sessions, both calibrations: Page CUSUM baseline on the window score, per-role (server/client) thresholds, quantile-defined fast path (eps_f = 0.1 %)

items.comment: Mitigation objective ranks by bit rate but the solver ranks by packet-rate thresholds and source score; Q missing from goodput and zero-collateral constraint; equivalence only while overloaded; joint vs separate budgets.
items.response: Eq. (4) now applies the quarantine to legitimate traffic too; Eq. (5) adds the constraint that no quarantined port is bound to a legitimate host; the equivalence to minimising residual load is stated as holding only while the link is overloaded; the solver's score ranking is stated as a confidence heuristic (cap never reached in our runs); separate rule and quarantine budgets in the implementation are stated.

items.comment: Pre-split label snooping (conflicting-label rows removed over the whole dataset).
items.response: Fixed: conflicts are now removed inside the training split only and the holdouts keep all rows. Re-evaluated all models: combined HGB 0.914 / 0.919 (was 0.976 / 0.948), cross-dataset 0.485 / 0.618 with ROC-AUC 0.533 / 0.786. Abstract, Fig. 2, Table II and text updated.
items.where: Sec. V-A, VI-A, Fig. 2, Table II, Abstract

items.comment: Pooled role calibration gives 24-30 % benign FPR on the victim; test stratified thresholds offline.
items.response: Evaluated per-role thresholds offline: the server threshold rises to about 1.0 and F1 collapses to 0.02-0.24, showing the server false positives are intrinsic to the window features, not only a pooling artefact. Eq. (3) now states that the H0 probability is pooled over destinations.
items.status: Resolved (new analysis); remedy left as future work

items.comment: Fast-path threshold inversion when eta is recalibrated (eta = 0.980 > eta_f = 0.97).
items.response: eta_f is now defined as the (1 - eps_f) quantile with eps_f = 0.1 % < eps, so eta_f > eta by construction; offline at 25 Mbit/s this gives eta_f = 0.998 and lowers false-alarm episodes from 44-63 to 30-43 per hour with all episodes detected in 3.2-4.2 s. The runs reported in Sec. VI-B to E are labelled as using the fixed 0.97.
items.where: Sec. III-D, VI-G, VI-H, Table XI

items.comment: Counter-based attribution is blind under packet-in saturation and for low-rate attackers.
items.response: Stated explicitly in Sec. IV-C and the limitations, with per-(s, d) packet-in counting proposed as the fix; low-rate attackers are reported as detected but not attributed.

items.comment: No CUSUM baseline for the confirmation heuristic.
items.response: Added a one-sided Page CUSUM on the same window score with h matched on calibration. It gives a similar delay vs false-alarm trade-off; the paper now says the 2-of-3 rule is not better than standard sequential detection, only more transparent.
items.where: Sec. V-C, VI-H, Table XI, Conclusion
